question: You will see one image. Which of these is it most likely to be? (a) a frame from a top-budget film, a AAA game cinematic or a cinema nature documentary, (b) a stock photograph, (c) a seed catalog or textbook picture, (d) amateur generated art, (e) a real-time web 3D demo. Answer with one letter, a confidence from 0 to 100, and the one thing that most influenced your answer.

votes.answer: e, 76/100: The evenly slanted rain streaks look like a real-time particle effect layered across the scene.

(e), 92 — The visible low-poly 3D geometry and instanced meshes, especially the identical sharp-edged grass tufts and polygonal plant stem intersecting cleanly into a displaced heightmap terrain alongside uniform particle-streak rain.

Answer: (a). Confidence: 50. What swayed me most: it looks like a deliberately cinematic CG render. It has a filmic widescreen frame, moody storm grading, shallow depth of field, a backlit rim-glow on the fuzzy stem and leaves, and rain-streak motion blur. That reads as a high-end cinematic shot, not a stock photo, catalog picture or real-time web demo. The main pull toward (d) is a few weak spots: the plant's anatomy is slightly off (one dark leaf floats loose behind the stem) and the rain streaks are very uniform.
e, 80/100. The uniformly angled rain streaks look like a real-time particle effect.
a 76 The stem hairs read as groomed geometric strands with even cinematic rim light, not photo fuzz or a simple web-demo card.
a, 72/100. The fine rim lighting that picks out individual hairs along the foreground stem most influenced my answer.

e, 92 — Real-time WebGL/post-processing depth-of-field and low-poly mesh artifacts: the cloned, low-poly midground stalks are blurred while the procedural noise-displaced mountain ridge and 1-pixel skybox stars behind them stay sharp, paired with visible polygonal leaf facets and 1-pixel edge aliasing on the hero plant.

a, 65. Cinematic 16:9 widescreen framing with a rim-lit, finely detailed hairy sunflower seedling against the Milky Way, shallow depth of field and graded teal night tones. It reads like a frame from a high-end nature documentary (or a polished CG render), not a stock photo or textbook shot.
a, 82/100. The precise rim lighting that picks out individual hairs on the foreground stem most influenced my answer.
a 74 The theatrical rim light on the plant’s fine hairs against the Milky Way makes it a directed cinematic frame.
e, 83 — The same angular sunflower models appear to repeat across the field like instanced 3D assets.
e, 88, the visibly low-poly faceted leaf geometry and repetitive instanced 3D sunflower and grass meshes across a flat terrain plane with contradicting directional fill lighting.

d — confidence 40. Main factor: this is clearly a CG render, with instanced, repeated sunflower models and grass cards. The lighting is inconsistent: the sun is behind the field, yet the flower heads and leaves are front-lit. The overall look is polished, with grain, volumetric haze and grading, so it reads like a hobbyist Blender/Unreal scene rather than top-budget film, AAA or documentary work. A real-time web demo (e) is the next most likely answer.
e, 80, the same sunflower shapes repeat across the field like instanced 3D assets.
e, 82, angular low-poly leaf edges and flat billboard grass on the foreground plants
